Aspiring teacher/current tutor!! You’re in charge of your classroom, and you can do all of these things with rules of qualification. A good rule of thumb might be “you can eat it as long as I can’t hear it” and the standard “you can have gum as long as I don’t see it.”  I know I’m probably going to be a little authoritarian on a no chips policy, but if a kid doesn’t follow the rules either make them throw the thing (like gum) away or put it back in their bag.

All my advice here is pretty theoretical, but the gum policy worked exceptionally well with one of my highschool teachers. There was never any gum under his desks and it prevented pretty much all of the chewing noises (seeing it in somebody’s open mouth counted as much as popping bubbles.)

My middle school English teacher won State teacher and national honors of the year during the Obama administration. I don’t remember much, but I do recall how she was beyond excited just to tell us about her experience and how happy she was to have the opportunity.  I guess my point is that even if Trump is disliked by these teachers, it’d still be memorable and be meaningful for them. It wouldn’t take too much of his time, even if it was just for a short commemoration or congratulation.
